edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De resurrectione carnis, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.locus: On the Resurrection of the Flesh LXIII
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Resurget igitur caro, et quidem omnis, et quidem ipsa, et quidem integra. In deposito est ubicumque apud Deum, per fidelissimum sequestrem Dei et hominum Jesum Christum, qui et homini Deum, et hominem Deo reddet, carni spiritum, et spiritui carnem. Utrumque jam in semetipso faederavit, sponsam sponso, et sponsum sponsae comparavit. Nam et si animam quis contenderit sponsam, vel dotis nomine sequetur animam caro. Non erit anima prostituta, ut nuda suscipiatur a sponso: habet instrumentum, habet cultum, habet mancipium suum carnem; ut collactanea comitabitur. Sed caro est sponsa, quae et in Christo Jesu spiritum sponsum per sanguinem pacta est. Hujus interitum quem putas, secessum scias esse. Non sola anima seponitur; habet et caro secessus suos interim, in aquis, in ignibus, in alitibus, in bestiis. Cum in haec dissolvi videtur, velut in vasa transfunditur. Si etiam ipsa vasa defecerint, cum de illis quoque effluxerit, in suam matricem terram quasi per ambages resorbetur, ut rursus ex illa repraesentetur Adam, auditurus a Domino: Ecce Adam quasi unus ex nobis factus est: vere tunc compos mali quod evasit, et boni quod invasit. Quid, anima, invides carni? nemo tam proximus tibi, quem post Dominum diligas: nemo magis frater tuus, quae tecum etiam in Deo nascitur. Tu potius illi exorare debueras resurrectionem; per te, si forte, deliquit. Sed nihil mirum si odisti, cujus auctorem quoque respuisti; quam et in Christo, aut negare, aut mutare consuevisti. Proinde et ipsum Sermonem Dei, qui caro factus est, vel stylo vel interpretatione corrumpens, arcana etiam apocryphorum superducens, blasphemiae fabulas. At enim Deus omnipotens, adversus haec incredulitatis et perversitatis ingenia providentissima gratia sua effundens in novissimis diebus de suo Spiritu in omnem carnem, in servos suos et ancillas, et fidem laborantem resurrectionis carnalis animavit, et pristina instrumenta manifestis verborum et sensuum luminibus, ab omni ambiguitatis obscuritate purgavit. Nam quia haereses esse oportuerat, ut probabiles quique manifestarentur; hae autem sine aliquibus occasionibus Scripturarum audere non poterant; idcirco pristina instrumenta quasdam materias illis videntur subministrasse, et ipsas quidem iisdem literis revincibiles. Sed, quoniam nec dissimulare Spiritum Sanctum oportebat, quo minus et ejusmodi eloquiis superinundaret, quae nullis haereticorum versutiis semina subspargerent, imo et veteres eorum cespites vellerent; idcirco jam omnes retro ambiguitates, et quas volunt parabolas, aperta atque perspicua totius sacramenti praedicatione discussit, per novam prophetiam de Paracleto inundantem; cujus si hanseris fontes, nullam poteris sitire doctrinam, nullus te ardor exuret quaestionum; resurrectionem quoque carnis usquequaque potando, refrigerabis.
pass_a_gloss: The flesh will rise again, and indeed all of it, and indeed the very same, and indeed whole. It is on deposit wherever with God, through the most faithful mediator of God and men Jesus Christ, who will also restore God to man and man to God, spirit to flesh, and flesh to spirit. He has already pledged both in Himself, the bride to the bridegroom and the bridegroom to the bride. For even if someone contends that the soul is the bride, the flesh will also follow the soul by right of dowry. The soul will not be prostituted so as to be received naked by the bridegroom: it has its instrument, it has its cultivation, it has its own property, the flesh, so that it may be accompanied by its nursling. But the flesh is the bride, which has also been pledged to the spirit, the bridegroom, through the blood of Christ. You think this is its destruction, know that it is its separation. Not only the soul is separated; the flesh also has its own separations in the meantime, in waters, in fires, in birds, in beasts. When it seems to be dissolved into these things, it is as if poured into vessels. If even these vessels fail, when it has flowed out from them, it will be absorbed back into its own matrix, the earth, as if through winding ways, so that Adam may be represented again from it, and may hear from the Lord: Behold, Adam has become as one of us. Truly then he will be composed of the evil that he escaped and the good that he invaded. Why, soul, do you envy the flesh? No one is as close to you as the one you love after the Lord: no one is more your brother, who is also born with you in God. You ought to have rather begged for resurrection for it; through you, perhaps, it sinned. But it is no wonder if you hate it, whose author you have also rejected; whom you are also accustomed to deny or change in Christ. And so you also corrupt the very Word of God, who was made flesh, either with the pen or with interpretation, and introduce secret and apocryphal things, fables of blasphemy. But God, omnipotent, pouring out His most provident grace against these minds of unbelief and perversity in the last days, from His Spirit into all flesh, into His servants and handmaids, and into the faith that labors for the resurrection of the flesh, has given life, and has purified the former instruments from all obscurity of ambiguity with the manifest light of words and senses. For since heresies had to exist, so that those who are approved might be made manifest, and these heresies could not dare without some occasions from the Scriptures, therefore the former instruments seem to have supplied some materials to them, and indeed with the same letters they can be refuted. But since it was not necessary to hide the Holy Spirit, so that He might not overflow with such speeches, which would not scatter seeds for the cunning of heretics, but rather would root out their old plots, therefore He has now discussed all former ambiguities and the parables they wish, with the open and clear preaching of the whole sacrament, through the new prophecy that overflows from the Paraclete; if you drink from its fountains, you will not be able to thirst for any doctrine, no heat of questions will burn you; also, by drinking the resurrection of the flesh everywhere, you will be refreshed.

bible_refs.note: Behold, Adam has become as one of us

pass_b_english: The flesh will rise again—all of it, the very same flesh, and whole. It is on deposit with God, wherever that may be, held by the most faithful mediator of God and humanity, Jesus Christ, who will restore God to humanity and humanity to God, spirit to flesh and flesh to spirit. He has already pledged both in himself: the bride to the bridegroom and the bridegroom to the bride. Even if someone argues that the soul is the bride, the flesh will still follow the soul by right of dowry. The soul will not be prostituted by being received naked by the bridegroom; it has its instrument, its cultivation, its own property—the flesh—so that it may be accompanied by its nursling. But the flesh is the bride, and she has been pledged to the spirit, the bridegroom, through the blood of Christ. You think this is her destruction? Know that it is only her separation. Not only the soul is separated; the flesh has its own separations for now—in waters, in fires, in birds, in beasts. When it seems to dissolve into these, it is merely poured like liquid into vessels. Even if those vessels fail, once the flesh has flowed out of them, it will be absorbed back into its matrix, the earth, by winding paths, so that Adam may be formed from it once more, hearing from the Lord: "Behold, Adam has become like one of us" (Gen. 3:22). Then he will truly be composed of the evil he escaped and the good he invaded.

Why, soul, do you envy the flesh? No one is closer to you, the one you must love after the Lord; no one is more your brother, the one born with you in God. You ought to have pleaded for its resurrection; through you, perhaps, it sinned. But it is no wonder you hate it, since you have also rejected its Author—whom you are accustomed to deny or alter in Christ. And so you corrupt the very Word of God who became flesh, whether by pen or by interpretation, dragging in secret apocryphal fables of blasphemy. But God Almighty, pouring out his most provident grace against these minds of unbelief and perversity in the last days, has sent his Spirit into all flesh, into his servants and handmaids, and into the faith that labors for the resurrection of the flesh, giving it life. He has purified the former instruments from every obscurity of ambiguity by the manifest light of words and senses. Since heresies had to exist so that the approved might be revealed, and since heresies could not dare to arise without some occasion from the Scriptures, the former instruments seem to have supplied them with some materials—materials that can be refuted by those very same letters. Yet the Holy Spirit could not be hidden, lest such speeches overflow without scattering any seed for the cunning of heretics, but rather uproot their old plots. Therefore he has now cleared away all former ambiguities and the parables they prefer, through the open and clear preaching of the whole sacrament, by the new prophecy overflowing from the Paraclete. If you drink from its fountains, you will thirst for no doctrine; no heat of questions will burn you; by drinking the resurrection of the flesh everywhere, you will be refreshed.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful clause-by-clause translation. Pass B is a fluent rendering that maintains the meaning and includes the required scripture citation (Gen. 3:22) for the allusion 'Ecce Adam quasi unus ex nobis factus est'.
